digest.component_or_area: MCP serving endpoint and health monitoring
propositions: MCP container was OOM-killed ~3min into a plan-review gate run on an 8GiB t4g.large host, causing the process to exit with status 137
nginx upstream pointed at the dead container port with no failover, converting a transient crash into a persistent HTTP 502 that persisted ~12 hours with no self-recovery
The system had no observability for MCP endpoint health; no mcp_healthy metric existed and /mcp was unreachable from outside the box, so the 502 was detected only by human report
mcp_retire_sweep in autodeploy.sh reaped exited-but-live containers while nginx still named their ports because the live-backend guard sat only in the Running branch, not the else arm

In-process gate execution causes the gate's memory footprint to be the MCP server's memory, with unbounded fan-out (two pools of 6 parallel LLM calls) and no per-container memory limits on any service

With the retire-sweep guard fixed and container healthchecks in place, transient MCP crashes now recover in ~30s instead of requiring 12-hour manual intervention, but the underlying OOM condition during long gate runs remains unresolved
